About
About us
Spórt-Ionad Réigiúnach Chorcaí Cuideachta Faoi Theorainn Rathaíochta, established in 1997, manages and operates recreational facilities in Cork on behalf of Cork City Council.
Currently, it oversees five facilities: LeisureWorld Bishopstown, LeisureWorld Churchfield, LeisureWorld Douglas, Mahon Golf Course, and St. Peter’s Cork.
LeisureWorld Bishopstown
LeisureWorld Bishopstown
was opened in 1997. This is the flag ship LW Management site and its largest facility. It has 3 swimming pools (25m, 18m and toddler pool), 2 gyms (main fully equipped gym & speciality gym), class studios, outdoor astro turf pitches as well as a busy on site café, all located in Bishopstown, Cork.
LeisureWorld Churchfield
In 2005 LW Management then took over a facility on the North side of the city which is now called
LeisureWorld Churchfield
. This facility is the second largest of the LeisureWorld facilities and has a special place in the community with a strong family focus. It has 3 pools (25m, children’s pool and toddler pool with play zone), a large water slide, 2 gyms (Dedicated free weights gym, main fitness gym), class studios and outdoor astro turf pitches.
LeisureWorld Douglas
LW Management took over the management of the Gus Healy Swimming Pools in Douglas in 2012 on behalf of Cork City Council.
LeisureWorld Douglas
has one 25m pool. This is a very busy pool for children’s swimming lessons as well as swim club rental and as a result, public swimming times are limited.
Mahon Golf Course
Mahon Golf Course
is Ireland’s first purpose made Municipal Golf Course. In 1978 Cork City Council commissioned Mr. Eddie Hacket to design an 18 hole golf course on the Mahon peninsula. This was to be Irelands first purpose made Municipal Golf Course and was financially assisted by the Golfing Union of Ireland.
The course was officially opened on 3rd September 1980 and was called the Ted McCarthy Municipal Golf Course. The course is renowned to provide a very challenging test to all grade of golfer.
St. Peter’s Cork
The newest and most diverse site in LW Management’s portfolio is
St. Peter’s Cork
. An exhibition and event centre located on North Main Street, St.Peter’s Cork has historical roots dating back to medieval times. A deconsecrated Church, this public exhibition centre is open to all visitors 6 days a week.
LW Management took over the management of St. Peter’s Cork in 2016. The venue is a popular event space in Cork city and plays host to a variety of talks, workshops, performances and indoor markets. It also plays host to a number of private events such as corporate events and weddings.

This Cookie Policy was last updated on October 5, 2020 and applies to citizens and legal permanent residents of the European Economic Area and Switzerland.
1. Introduction
Our website,
https://www.leisureworldcork.com
(hereinafter: "the website") uses cookies and other related technologies (for convenience all technologies are referred to as "cookies"). Cookies are also placed by third parties we have engaged. In the document below we inform you about the use of cookies on our website.
2. What are cookies?
A cookie is a small simple file that is sent along with pages of this website and stored by your browser on the hard drive of your computer or another device. The information stored therein may be returned to our servers or to the servers of the relevant third parties during a subsequent visit.
3. What are scripts?
A script is a piece of program code that is used to make our website function properly and interactively. This code is executed on our server or on your device.
4. What is a web beacon?
A web beacon (or a pixel tag) is a small, invisible piece of text or image on a website that is used to monitor traffic on a website. In order to do this, various data about you is stored using web beacons.
5. Cookies
5.1 Technical or functional cookies
Some cookies ensure that certain parts of the website work properly and that your user preferences remain known. By placing functional cookies, we make it easier for you to visit our website. This way, you do not need to repeatedly enter the same information when visiting our website and, for example, the items remain in your shopping cart until you have paid. Accessibility
LeisureWorld Disability Inclusion Policy
The mission of LeisureWorld is to value the abilities and individuality of people with disabilities by providing opportunities for them to reach their full potential within an inclusive culture. At LeisureWorld, we will achieve disability inclusion by:
Continuously reviewing our approach, which involves members, staff, and management.
Partnering with clubs, disability services, and consulting with people with disabilities and their families.
This ensures that our organisation is inclusive for everyone. We welcome all community members, regardless of their abilities, and strive to include people with disabilities in both playing and non-playing roles as fully as possible.
Our Commitments:
Legislation Compliance:
We are committed to complying with the Equal Status Acts 2000-2012, the Disability Act 2005, and Article 30.5 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities.
Sports Inclusion:
We fulfill the requirements of the Sports Ireland Policy on Participation in Sport by People with Disabilities and engage with the Sport Inclusion Disability Charter.
Accessibility:
We aim to make our environment, clubs, training, and facilities accessible to people with disabilities. We consider reasonable adjustments to achieve this goal effectively.
Facilities and Services:
Parking:
We have disability parking spaces directly outside LeisureWorld entrance.
Pool:
Our pool has steps leading into the shallow end or we have use of a hoist.
Changing Rooms:
Accessible changing rooms with showers and toilets are available. These are easily accessible from the pool changing area and provide direct access to the pool.
Staff Assistance:
Our trained staff, including lifeguards, are available to assist with entering and exiting the water.
Gym Access:
The gym is accessible via lifts. It features wide spaces and brightly colour contrasted equipment. Wheelchair-accessible equipment includes:
Dual Adjustable Pulley:
For various strength training exercises.
Ski Erg:
For cardio and strength work with adjustable resistance.
Assault Bike:
Usable with arms only, legs only, or both for cardio.
Free Weights:
Suitable for standing or sitting exercises.
Upper arm Ergometer:
For cardio with removable seat for wheelchair access.
Our Goals:
By enhancing our capacity and capabilities, we strive to deliver inclusive programs, advocate for disability inclusion, and increase participation by people with disabilities in our sports and organisation.
Our Actions:
Inclusive Approach:
We will adopt an inclusive approach across all aspects of the organisation by consulting with our members.
Consultation:
We will listen to the voices of people with disabilities in all our deliberations and program development.
Partnerships:
We will work with other organisations and advocates for disability inclusion.
Governance:
We will promote good governance to ensure the participation of people with disabilities.
Recognition:
We will acknowledge and support the contributions, achievements, and successes of people with disabilities in our organisation.
Commitment:
We commit to adopting the Sport Inclusion Disability Charter.
We will review our Disability Inclusion Policy annually to meet the requirements of each individual and provide them with the opportunities they need to reach their full potential.
LeisureWorld strives to provide accessible leisure opportunities catering for a wide range of levels and abilities. The following are some of the features which may be of particular interest to our visitors with accessibility requirements.
Parking
Our accessible parking is located at the entrance of LeisureWorld for customer use only
Lift
The lift is located near the gym and provides access to gym & studios.
Toilets
We provide accessible toilets in the main reception, changing village and gym area. Our toilets are also equipped with baby changing facilities.
Showers
We have both accessible showers in the changing village and gym area.
Changing Area

Where is the programme delivered?
The programme is delivered in the functional training zone in Leisureworld Bishosptown. These are two leisure centres operated by Cork City Council located in Bishopstown and Churchfield, Cork. This is a not for profit organisation.
Who are the clients?
People who have
1. had a single neurological event e.g. stroke, acquired brain injury, spinal cord injury etc resulting in physical impairment .
2. People who have progressive chronic neurological conditions e. g. Parkinsons, Multiple Sclerosis etc
Pathways – How are people referred and what happens next?
At present, the pathway for access to the Functional Zone is via the HSE Community Physiotherapy service only.

This is a mixed class tailored to individuals who would like a fun way to get cardio into your day. If you want an exciting and fun cardio full body 45 minutes workout class, this class is for you! Participants must be able to exercise independently without the use of a mobility aid. To begin, each participant will do twenty minutes on any two or more cardio machines of their choice. Adult & Children Swimming Lessons Cork
Daunted by swimming? Have you ever considered swimming lessons? Whether you’re a total beginner or want to improve your swimming stroke, at the LeisureWorld Swim School in Cork we have swimming lessons for all ages and abilities. Adult lessons are fun, enjoyable and structured to enable the individual swimmer to learn at his/her own pace.
Each person is assessed at the beginning of the course and is advised of which class will suitably reflect their ability so they are learning alongside adults of the same standard. We feel this is the best way to teach swimming as it allows you the opportunity to progress at your own pace.
Click adult or children’s lessons below to read more.

These are available at different times throughout the year, please contact your local LeisureWorld Facility to see when the next course is starting.

Children's Swimming Lessons
Understand Our Courses at LeisureWorld
At LeisureWorld Bishopstown, we offer
three main swimming programs
tailored to suit different skill levels and interests:
Water Safety and Fun
: A beginner-level program for children aged 5 and above, focusing on water confidence, safety, and basic swimming techniques.
Swimming Skills
: An advanced program for passionate swimmers, designed to refine strokes, build endurance, and prepare for competitive-style swimming.
Rookie Lifeguard Classes
: A specialised program teaching lifesaving and rescue skills, ideal for children interested in learning essential water safety techniques.
Read on to learn more about each program and find the perfect fit for your child!
Water Safety and Fun
Our
Water Safety and Fun
program is designed for beginners, perfect for children aged 5 and above who have little to no prior swimming experience. This course introduces kids to swimming and gradually builds their skills in a safe and enjoyable environment.
Key competencies covered include:
Learning water safety in shallow and deep areas.
Mastering fundamental swim strokes: front crawl, back crawl, and breaststroke.
Engaging in fun and interactive water activities.
The program consists of four progressive levels:
Starfish, Penguins, Turtles, and Dolphins.
Each level focuses on specific skills and milestones. Children progress at their own pace, advancing to the next level only when they achieve the required competencies.
Main Goals of Each Level
Starfish: Ages 5 -7 years old
This level helps children build confidence in the water and introduces basic water skills.
Putting their face in the water.
Floating on their front and back.
Gliding through the water with confidence.
Penguins: 5 – 9 year olds
At this stage, children adapt to larger pools, strengthen their coordination, and extend their water skills.
Getting comfortable in a big pool.
Kicking their legs to swim longer distances.
Swimming on their back (belly up).
Retrieving objects from the bottom of the pool.
Swimming through hoops.
Turtles: 6 – 10 year olds
This level emphasises advanced swimming techniques and deep-water safety.
Using arms for all swimming strokes.
Treading water effectively.
Safely jumping and diving in the deep end.
Swimming full strokes (front crawl, back crawl).
Introducing breaststroke.
Dolphins:
The final stage focuses on long-distance swimming and deep-water confidence.
Mastering breathing techniques for all strokes.
Staying confidently in the deep end for the entire class.
Perfecting the breaststroke kick and timing.
Swimming longer distances in all strokes.
Retrieving objects from deep water.
Performing kneeling and standing dives.
Upon completing the
Dolphins
level, your child will graduate from Water Safety and Fun.
What’s Next After Graduation?
If your child loves swimming and wishes to advance further, they can join our
Swimming Skills
program. This course is for passionate swimmers and focuses on:
Practicing lane swimming.
Perfecting all four main strokes: front crawl, back crawl, breaststroke, and butterfly.
Learning starts, turns, and diving techniques.
Building endurance and speed.

: 8–12 years old.
Sharks 2
: 8–15 years old.
After completing
Swimming Skills

LeisureWorld Sharks Swim Club
, which focuses on competitive-style lane swimming.

While it’s not an official swim club for competitions, it’s an excellent pathway for future competitive swimmers.

Rookie Lifeguard Classes

Key skills taught include:
Lifesaving swimming strokes.
Safely towing individuals out of the water.
Administering CPR and using an AED.
First-aid techniques like bandaging.
Recognising and assisting different types of casualties.

FAQs
Assessments FAQ
How do I enroll my child in swimming lessons?
Before your child can be enrolled, an assessment needs to be completed. During this assessment, our swim instructors will evaluate not only your child’s abilities in the water but also how comfortable they are in the pool environment without their guardian being present. Afterward, the instructor will inform you of the most appropriate level for your child based on our competencies. Then, you can visit the reception, where they will be ready to enroll your child in one of our groups.
What do I need to bring for the assessment?
For the assessment, your child needs to wear their swimming gear, including a swimsuit, swim cap, and goggles (goggles are optional for the assessment but mandatory for the lessons). Don’t forget to bring a towel and any extra clothing items needed for after the assessment.
How long is the assessment?
The assessment itself takes no longer than 5 minutes, but you may need to wait for your child to be called by one of our teachers, as there could be a queue. It is the parent’s responsibility to stay on-site for the entire duration of the assessment and any necessary waiting time. Parents should remain in the shower area to hand their child over to the instructor, collect them afterward, and receive further instructions from the assessor.
What does my child need to start swimming lessons?
Your child does not need any previous swimming experience but must be at least 5 years old to enroll in our swimming school. Additionally, they need to be within the age range for our classes. This is because our learner’s pool is not suitable for older or taller children, and the shallow end of the main pool may be too small for them.
What if my child has a learning disability or any medical condition?
If your child has a learning disability or medical condition, please inform our reception staff when enrolling, so they can record the information. This will help the swim instructors tailor the lessons appropriately.
FAQ on Swim Lessons
My child has just finished Dolphins. Can they move to Sharks immediately?
No. The “Water Safety and Fun” course (Starfish, Penguins, Turtles, and Dolphins) and the “Swimming Skills” course (Sharks 1 and 2) are separate courses with different goals and skill levels. Once your child completes all competencies in the Water Safety and Fun group, they will graduate from that course. If, after finishing Dolphins, your child wants to further improve their technique, stamina, and
distance, we recommend contacting our reception team to check availability in the Swimming Skills course.
When will my child be ready to move to the next level?
Each child develops at their own pace and will progress through competencies in their own time. To track their progress, use the LeisureWorld app, where you can see if they have passed each competency. Once all competencies have been passed, the instructor will wait a couple of weeks to ensure the child can consistently perform all requirements before moving them up to the next level. This ensures they will be comfortable in the next group.
My child isn’t moving up, and I believe they have been in a group for too long. What should I do?
Half an hour of practice a week can only take you so far. Your child can swim for free at LeisureWorld as long as they are enrolled in classes. We recommend bringing them for extra swims to help them get more practice and become more comfortable with their swimming skills. This will support their progress, so we encourage parents to bring their children for extra practice as often as possible. Remember, you play an important role in your child’s progress.
Can I watch my child’s swimming lessons?
Yes, you should! Our facility has a viewing gallery where parents can watch the lessons. Please drop your child off at the shower area, then go around to reception to enter the viewing gallery. 5 minutes before the class ends, parents should return to the shower area to assist their child.
How do I know if my child is progressing?
To track your child’s progress, use the LeisureWorld app to view their competencies and see if they have passed them. Please note that if your child misses several lessons, some competencies they previously passed may be marked as “not passed” again. Be sure to keep bringing them to class to maintain progress.
